knowledge_point.title: Applying the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals Over Parametric Curves

question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=2 x y^{2} + x y z.$ Given that $C$ is the path along the curve $r(t)=⟨e^{t},t + 2,e^{- t}⟩$ for $t\in [0,1],$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a piecewise-smooth curve given by the vector function $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b].$ Let $f$ be a differentiable function of two or three variables such that $∇f$ is continuous on $C.$ The fundamental theorem for line integrals states that 

$$
{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r=f(r(b))-f(r(a)).
$$

 

In our case, the position vectors of the endpoints of the curve are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨1,2,1⟩ \\ r(1) & =⟨e,3,e^{-1}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the endpoints of the path defined by $C$ are $(1,2,1)$ and $(e,3,e^{-1}).$

Applying the fundamental theorem for line integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}∇f\cdot \text{d}r & =f(r(1))-f(r(0)) \\  & =f(e,3,e^{-1})-f(1,2,1) \\  & =\left(2 \left(e\right) \left(3\right)^{2} + \left(e\right) \left(3\right) \left(e^{-1}\right)\right)-\left(2 \left(1\right) \left(2\right)^{2} + \left(1\right) \left(2\right) \left(1\right)\right) \\  & =\left(3 + 18 e\right)-\left(10\right) \\  & =-7 + 18 e.\end{aligned}
$$
